concept: Slider is the fader on the face of an appliance. A plastic cap rides a recessed groove under a printed ruler scale, follows the hand and settles into the nearest detent on the material's spring, while the orange stays on the unit's rotary.

default_to_avoid.pattern: thin Material or iOS slider with a coloured filled track and a round white thumb
default_to_avoid.why_not: A coloured fill spends the accent on a secondary control, while P1 keeps orange for the rotary and P3 asks for a cap riding a groove under a ruler scale.

default_to_avoid.pattern: range slider that shrinks to its label or grows with its value text
default_to_avoid.why_not: P6 keeps positions fixed between states, so the fader holds its length and size from its lowest value to its highest (gate G-SL1).

references.source: Braun audio 1 / audio 2 compact systems (Dieter Rams, 1962): linear faders in a slot with a printed ruler scale and numerals under it
Braun TG 60 tape recorder (Dieter Rams, 1965): level faders with plain rectangular caps and an ink index line
apps/lab/anchor (D-001, card A): the volume fader with 11 detents on the ruler

derivation.consequence: faders ride a groove with a ruler scale
derivation.form: A recessed groove runs the full length of the control, with ruler ticks printed above it and an optional row of numerals printed below.

derivation.consequence: rotaries and faders settle into the nearest detent
derivation.form: The cap follows the pointer while dragged and, when released, travels to the nearest step on a spring of mass 1.4, stiffness 520 and damping 46.

derivation.consequence: scale numerals on a fader are tabular, the smallest size step, ink at ≥4.5:1
derivation.form: Ruler numerals are type.micro in medium weight with tabular figures, in text.secondary ink on the plastic body.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The cap is surface.raised plastic with a printed ink line and the groove is surface.sunken, so no part of the fader uses action.accent.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The fader takes the full inline size of its column, at least five touch targets long, and its value text never changes the track length.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: The track is a role slider: arrows step one detent, PageUp and PageDown a larger step, Home and End the ends, with the printed label and value above it.

options.name: ruler fader: ticks above a narrow groove, numerals below
channel fader: the whole track is a wide well with the cap inside
notch rail: a recessed notch per detent and a round cap that drops between them

variants.reason: A is the fader of anchor card A and P3's groove with a ruler scale, and it keeps the recess narrow so the display stays the deepest window (P2); B's 44px well competes with the display, and C's notch rail only reads with a few steps and drops the free travel of a fader.

root.why: The fader fills the inline size of its column and keeps at least five touch targets of length in every state.

header.why: The label and the value sit on one printed line above the track, aligned to its two ends.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the word printed above a fader on a case.

value.why: The current value is printed with tabular figures so the digits do not shift sideways while the cap moves.

fader.why: The whole track is the hit area and stays at least 44px tall although the groove itself draws narrower.

rule.why: The ruler band above the groove holds one printed tick per detent, spanning the travel of the cap's centre.

tick.why: Each tick is a hairline of printing, flat on the material with no shadow, so it never reads as a part.

major.why: The ends and the middle of the ruler are printed in the primary ink so the scale can be read at a glance.

groove.why: The cap rides a narrow recessed slot drawn with inverse light, the groove every fader on the case runs in; its hairline edge in line.ring holds 3:1 against the body in both themes.

cap.why: The cap is a raised part of the same plastic, casting the short part shadow down and to the right of the single light.

scale.why: The optional numeral row under the groove prints the scale values in the smallest type step, as on the reference.

numeral.why: Each numeral is centred under its tick with tabular figures, in medium weight at the smallest size step.

hover.why: Hover darkens the cap's printed index one step and never lifts or grows the cap toward the pointer.

focus-visible.why: The keyboard focus ring wraps the whole track with the same dark ring every part in dial shows.

aria-disabled=true.why: A disabled fader loses the cap's height and fades to half, while the groove and ruler stay readable.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the cap jumps to its detent at once and the index ink changes with no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the cap, its index, the groove and the ticks are drawn as real borders in system colours.

border-color.why: The index ink step on hover comes in over 120ms and goes back over 240ms on the decelerating curve (motion.hover with kiln.state), fast in and slow out.
